Furthermore, the inclusion of irrelevant context distracts models from key details. records.title: PAINT: Parallel-in-time Neural Twins for Dynamical System Reconstruction
records.reason: PAINT models turbulent-fluid dynamics with parallel-in-time generative prediction; the contribution is physical-system forecasting, not LLM inference efficiency or infrastructure.
records.abstract_evidence_excerpt: Neural surrogates have shown great potential in simulating dynamical systems, while offering real-time capabilities. We envision Neural Twins as a progression of neural surrogates, aiming to create digital replicas of real systems. A neural twin consumes measurements at test time to update its state, thereby enabling context-specific decision-making. We argue, that a critical property of neural twins is their ability to remain on-trajectory, i.e., to stay close to the true system state over time. records.title: Video, How Do Your Tokens Merge?
records.reason: The paper measures training-free token merging for video vision transformers and video action-recognition accuracy/speed. It is an independent vision application rather than LLM inference infrastructure.
records.abstract_evidence_excerpt: Video transformer models require huge amounts of compute resources due to the spatio-temporal scaling of the input. Tackling this, recent methods have proposed to drop or merge tokens for image models, whether randomly or via learned methods. Merging tokens has many benefits: it can be plugged into any vision transformer, does not require model re-training, and it propagates information that would otherwise be dropped through the model. Before now, video token merging has not been evaluated on temporally complex datasets for video understanding. records.reason: Timed diarized transcript modeling targets real-time dialogue generation and reports token-rate requirements on commodity hardware, but it focuses on interaction modeling rather than a general inference optimization.
records.abstract_evidence_excerpt: Chatbots built upon language models have exploded in popularity, but they have largely been limited to synchronous, turn-by-turn dialogues. In this paper we present a simple yet general method to simulate real-time interactive conversations using pretrained text-only language models, by modeling timed diarized transcripts and decoding them with causal rejection sampling. We demonstrate the promise of this method with two case studies: instant messenger dialogues and spoken conversations, which require generation at about 30 tok/s and 20 tok/s respectively to maintain real-time interactivity. records.reason: PA-BDM combines parallel block diffusion and progressive KV caching to raise document-recognition throughput. The mechanism is a concrete inference optimization, but the application is document parsing rather than LLM systems.
records.abstract_evidence_excerpt: Block Diffusion Models (BDMs) support parallel generation, flexible-length output, and KV caching, making them promising for efficient document parsing. However, existing BDMs bind denoising and cache commitment to fixed block boundaries: parallelism shrinks during intra-block denoising, while generated tokens cannot be cached until the whole block is completed. records.reason: UniCo generates causal-reasoning training data and evaluates reasoning quality; its contribution is capability training without a runtime-efficiency result.
records.abstract_evidence_excerpt: Despite the importance of causal reasoning, training LLMs to reason causally remains underexplored. Existing data efforts mostly focus on benchmarking LLMs on specific aspects of causality, making them less suitable for training generalizable causal reasoners. To address this, we propose UniCo, a data generation framework that both (1) addresses 18 causal query types across Pearl's Causal Ladder and (2) translates natively symbolic examples into code and natural language forms to simulate real-world use cases where causal terms are not explicitly specified. records.abstract_evidence_excerpt: Serverless platforms offer compelling economics for low-traffic inference of small language models (SLMs), but cold start latency remains a critical barrier.
